title: observability: token-level KV & cost/latency dashboards + alert tuning
author: Ava Thompson
description: Add token-level KV cache, cost and latency metrics; add Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert tuning. Motivation: provide teams with actionable token-level breakdowns for cost and latency (hosted + dedicated) and surface KV cache health to avoid silent performance regressions. This PR: 1) Exposes new metrics from serving runtime: redwood_serving_token_latency_ms{model,route}, redwood_serving_token_cost_usd{model,route}, redwood_kv_cache_hit_ratio{pool}, redwood_kv_cache_miss_latency_ms{pool}, and redwood_serving_tokens_total{model,route}. 2) Adds tracing spans for token emit + kv lookup so traces correlate token latency with cache behavior. 3) Deploys two Grafana dashboards (TokenCostLatencyOverview, KVCacheHealth) and a compact combined dashboard for SRE runbooks. 4) Adds Prometheus alerting rules with tuned thresholds and severity levels; includes runbook links and auto-escalation policy notes. 5) Updates ownership annotations and docs (observability/README) with interpretation guidance and cost projection examples. Testing: unit + integration metrics tests; load experiment with 50k synthetic requests to validate percentiles and alert noise; manual verification of dashboards in staging. Checklist: - [x] expose metrics from runtime - [x] add traces + correlate IDs - [x] dashboard JSON + templating by region/model - [x] alert rules + runbooks - [x] document guidance and examples - [x] CI green after rerun. Related: ENG-4123 (token level observability epic), ENG-4199 (kv cache telemetry), SUP-88 (customer reported KV cache spike).

release_notes: Added token-level cost and latency metrics, KV cache health metrics, Grafana dashboards (TokenCostLatencyOverview, KVCacheHealth), and tuned Prometheus alerts with runbooks. This enables cost breakdowns by model/route and faster detection of KV cache induced latency regressions.
